_doc: Maps each supported artifact to its parser file, offline parser, output database, and (when available) its visual-anatomy reference page on https://crow-eye.com/eye-describe . The Eye Agent reads anatomy_url whenever it needs to explain the BINARY-LEVEL STRUCTURE of an artifact (offsets, field widths, signature bytes, on-disk layout). Knowledge .md files in this directory cover the SEMANTIC and FORENSIC questions; the anatomy pages cover the byte-level layout.

prefetch.description: Windows Prefetch file parser for program execution evidence
prefetch.anatomy_summary: Interactive byte-level walk of a .pf file: SCCA header, file version (Win 8/10/11 differences), executable name UTF-16 block, file metrics array, trace chains, volume info block with run_times array, and directory strings.

mft.description: Master File Table parser for NTFS file system metadata
mft.anatomy_summary: Byte-level walk of an MFT record: FILE0/FILE* signature, fixup array, sequence number, hard-link count, attribute list ($STANDARD_INFORMATION, $FILE_NAME, $DATA), MACB timestamps in $SIA vs $FNA streams, resident vs non-resident attributes, data runs.

amcache.description: AmCache (Amcache.hve) inventory parser - 29 tables. An inventory of what the Compatibility Appraiser has seen, not an execution log. Recovers entries DELETED from the hive out of free space, flags FileId hashes that are partial (only the first 30 MiB is hashed), and reports the Windows 7/8 Root\File schema as unparsed rather than returning nothing silently.
amcache.anatomy_summary: The inventory hive no HKEY points at: the keys under Root, what an InventoryApplicationFile entry holds, the four zeros in front of the SHA-1, and why an entry proves presence rather than execution.

shimcache.description: ShimCache (Application Compatibility Cache) parser - Windows 10/11 format only; older caches are named and refused rather than mis-parsed
shimcache.anatomy_summary: Byte-level walk of the AppCompatCache registry value: the header size that identifies the format, then per-record signature, per-record id, cell size, path length, path (UTF-16LE), last-modified FILETIME, data size, and the trailing data blob - an array of 12-byte (tag, type, value) slots carrying the executable's PE machine type and an operating-system-binary flag.

registry.table: 123 artifact tables in registry_data.db (AutoStartPrograms, UserAssist, Shellbags, startup_approved, registry_value_changes and others)
registry.description: Windows Registry hive parser. Covers persistence/ASEP keys (Winlogon, IFEO, AppInit_DLLs, Active Setup, per-user CLSID InprocServer32 shadowing, Command Processor AutoRun, Drivers32, SSODL, Browser Helper Objects, credential providers, netsh helper DLLs, AMSI providers, security providers, print monitors and processors, network providers, WMI autorecover MOFs and shell\open\command), security posture and anti-forensic settings (RDP-Tcp, usbstor Start, Windows Script Host, Explorer Advanced, FilesNotToSnapshot, event log channel config), device attribution (WPDBUSENUM, DeviceClasses, VolumeInfoCache), host identity (MachineGuid, ProductOptions, OS install history, system environment, network adapters, Group Policy history), per-user activity (FileExts, CIDSizeMRU, ProgramsCache, Regedit LastKey, printer connections), Scheduled Tasks from the SOFTWARE hive TaskCache, and UserAccounts - SAM merged with ProfileList, which maps a SID to a named user. Local group membership from SAM Builtin/Account Aliases, and the SECURITY hive (LSA policy, machine SID, primary domain, audit policy, LSA secret metadata, cached domain logon slots) - the live parser exports SAM and SECURITY with SeBackupPrivilege so both hives parse through the same code as an image case. LSA secrets are recorded by name and size only, never decrypted. Tables are named for the artifact, not the technique that abuses it. Transaction logs (.LOG1/.LOG2) are replayed into a temporary copy before an offline parse so a hive Windows had open is not read as final; the outcome per hive is recorded in registry_hive_state. Live and offline differences are documented in docs/live-vs-offline.md.
registry.anatomy_summary: Every registry artifact organised by the question it answers - execution, persistence, devices, user activity, machine identity - with live byte maps for the six value encodings that need binary parsing, and the full list of all 133 keys Crow-Eye reads.

usn.description: USN Journal parser for NTFS change log
usn.anatomy_summary: Byte-level walk of a USN journal record: record length, major/minor version, file reference number, parent reference number, USN sequence, timestamp, reason flags (FILE_CREATE / FILE_DELETE / RENAME bitmask), source info, security ID, file attributes, file-name length + UTF-16 name.

jumplist.description: Jump List and LNK file parser
jumplist.anatomy_summary: Three complementary pages. AutomaticDestinations: OLE compound document (MS-CFB) with DestList stream + per-entry LNK substreams. CustomDestinations: header + entry blocks each containing a full LNK shortcut. LNK Anatomy: ShellLinkHeader, LinkTargetIDList, LinkInfo, StringData (name/relative/working/arguments/icon), extra data blocks (Tracker, Console, EnvironmentVariableDataBlock, etc.).

recyclebin.anatomy_summary: Visual anatomy page not yet published.

srum.description: System Resource Usage Monitor parser. Output srum_data.db holds FIVE provider tables plus a bookkeeping table (there is no single 'srum_data' table): srum_application_usage (per-app, per-hour CPU + disk cost), srum_network_data_usage (bytes sent/received per app, per interface), srum_network_connectivity (interface connection windows), srum_energy_usage (battery charge + state; the short- and long-term energy providers merge here), srum_app_timeline (focus/keyboard/mouse seconds, duration, hosted_services; Windows 10+), and srum_metadata (one row per parse). Every provider row carries resolved app_name/app_path and user_sid/user_name (the numeric AppId/UserId resolved through SruDbIdMapTable). Timeline AppIds of the Store form (PackageFamily!PRAID!exe!timestamp!seq) resolve to the real executable. The parser also collects the ESE checkpoint set (SRU.chk, SRUDB.jfm, SRU*.log) so a dirty database is soft-recovered (esentutl /r) rather than repaired; srum_metadata records jfm_collected, log_files_collected and db_state (clean/recovered/repaired).
srum.anatomy_summary: Visual walkthrough of the SRUM ESE database (SRUDB.dat): its five provider tables, the SruDbIdMapTable that resolves App/User IDs to paths and SIDs, the hourly-window lifecycle and ~30-60 day retention, the checkpoint/log recovery model, and how Crow-Eye decodes the resource-usage rows.

eventlog.anatomy_summary: Visual anatomy page not yet published.

browser.description: Browser forensics parser for Chromium-family (Chrome, Edge, Brave, Chromium, Opera, Vivaldi), Gecko (Firefox), and Electron apps. One database with per-artifact tables (browser_history, browser_downloads, browser_cookies, browser_credentials, browser_autofill, browser_shortcuts, browser_network_predictor, browser_favicons, browser_bookmarks, browser_extensions, browser_preferences, browser_sessions, browser_local_storage, browser_indexeddb, browser_service_worker, browser_cache, browser_push, browser_media_router, browser_files, browser_metadata, and browser_gecko_* for Firefox). Every row carries provenance: browser, vendor, user_name, sid, profile, source_path. Cookie values and saved passwords are stored as base64 of the raw ENCRYPTED blob with an encryption_version (v10/v11/v20/dpapi) and are NEVER decrypted by the parser; the DPAPI-wrapped master key is kept in browser_metadata.os_crypt_key_b64 for a separate, audited decryption step. Full extraction copies HTTP cache bodies and IndexedDB blobs into browser_extracted/ with a browser_files inventory row (sha1, size, mtime). Live, offline-folder and forensic-image cases all produce the same 37 tables: collectors keep each profile tree at live_acquisition/Browser/<source>/Users/<name>/AppData/... (<source> = vol_<N>_<id> for an image partition, src_<folder>_<id> per imported source, live for Crow-Claw; <id> hashes the image or folder path so sources never merge), and offline_BrowserClaw takes user_name from that Users folder and sid from the evidence's own SOFTWARE hive ProfileList - empty when no hive was collected or when the case holds browser trees from more than one source - never from the analyst machine. On offline/image cases source_path is the copied file under live_acquisition/Browser, not the original drive path. The "Include browser cache" option (on by default) controls whether browser_cache / CacheStorage / Firefox cache2 are collected; when it is off those tables are empty by choice.
browser.anatomy_summary: Master-class guide to browser artifacts: how history, cookies, cache, sessions, saved logins and web-app storage work, where they live on disk, the difference between the Chromium and Gecko engines, and how Crow-Eye parses them.

anatomy_index._doc: Quick lookup: artifact_key -> anatomy_url. Use this when the user / agent asks 'how is artifact X structured at the byte level' — fetch the URL for a guided visual walkthrough.

consolidated_database.name: Log_Claw.db
consolidated_database.description: Consolidated database containing all parsed artifacts
consolidated_database.note: Alternative to querying individual artifact databases

shared_modules.registry_transaction_log.py: Replays a dirty hive's .LOG1/.LOG2 into a working copy before parsing. Used by every hive reader: offline_RegClaw, amcacheparser, offline_ShimCacheClaw, offline_SRUM_Claw, security_hive, user_identity. Amcache.hve has its own logs and is collected with them.
shared_modules.registry_hive_walk.py: Walks a hive's allocator rather than its tree, recovering class names, shared security descriptors, and keys and values still present in freed cells. Offline only: all three need the hive file.
